operationName: Ebola PHEIC Response — 2026 Bundibugyo Outbreak, DRC & Uganda
heroHeadline: Ebola Spreads to Sixth DRC Province as Africa CDC Warns Outbreak Could Become 'Largest in the World'
heroSubtitle: By 13 August 2026, the 2026 DRC-Uganda Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak reached 4,686 total lab-confirmed cases (4,665 DRC + 20 Uganda [outbreak closed] + 1 France) with 2,186 confirmed deaths (crude CFR ~46.8%), after a death in Buta, capital of the previously unaffected Bas-Uélé province, marked the outbreak's expansion to a sixth DRC province. Deaths rose from 1,000 to 2,000 in under a month — the fastest fatal surge in Ebola's recorded history. Africa CDC Director-General Dr. Jean Kaseya warned that without faster containment the outbreak 'will last more than a year and will be the largest in the world,' while WHO said it is on track to surpass the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (11,310 deaths) as the deadliest ever. Confirmed cases now sit just 35km from the South Sudan border. WHO and DRC are advancing talks to launch a Phase 3 ring-vaccination trial of Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) against Bundibugyo virus, for which no licensed vaccine exists.
footerNote: Data sourced from DRC Ministry of Health (MSANTE) situation reports, ECDC outbreak tracker, WHO Disease Outbreak News, Africa CDC statements, Uganda Ministry of Health, CDC Ebola Situation Summary, MSF, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Euronews, STAT News, and UN News. Case counts are rapidly evolving.
